title: Distinguish Linux utilization mount-identity failures from collection limits
outcome: Linux volume collection explains unrepresentable mount identities accurately and avoids unnecessary repeated mountinfo parsing within one sample.
acceptance: Invalid UTF-8 or control-character mount identities report an identity/probe failure; actual configured size/count limits retain a collection-limit reason and partial required-path metadata.
A single sampling round reuses a bounded mountinfo read for multiple volume paths, or records a reasoned decision to retain the existing cost.
Focused parsing/partial-collection tests cover invalid identity versus actual size limit without exposing failed configured paths or fabricating capacity.
